recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-24684 unless Patient Care opens a new issue about AdverseEvent.detected semantics or a different participant-function binding policy.
issue_request: FHIR-24684 was a Published Patient Care change request asking to rename AdverseEvent.detector to asserter and detected to assertedDate. The final Not Persuasive with Modification resolution removed detector, added AUT (Author) to the adverse-event participant-function value set, and explicitly did not rename detected because detector was folded into participant.
initial_application: The Jira-comment-linked commit af7e02d3f2258bf7df5ce33ffc9f0909d9514543 marked AdverseEvent.detector inactive in the then-authoritative spreadsheet and added AUT to valueset-adverse-event-participant-function. The 2021 source rework commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 carried the applied state forward into current StructureDefinition source.
additional_context: AdverseEvent is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/adverseevent/structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml and source/adverseevent/valueset-adverse-event-participant-function.xml are current build inputs. FHIR-16028 originally introduced AdverseEvent.detector, and Patient Care Confluence minutes corroborate that FHIR-24684 was resolved by removing detector. Follow-up Jira and Zulip searches found no later conflicting decision requiring detector to return or detected to be renamed.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source change was made because the current build-scope source already matches the final resolution.
